question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -15 \\ -15 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-19 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {3}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -9 & 9 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 18 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}22 & -15 \\ -15 & 13\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-19 \\ 24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=22+13+24=59.
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250894/assets/579e17e56674e39e552f1c0856f40e7f878ed94248a7a0e878c1f851c54ecbea.png)

What is the range of the function $f(x),$ shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the lowest and highest $y$-values in the graph.

- The lowest $y$-value is $-3.$ This occurs at the point $(3,-3).$

- The highest $y$-value is $1.$ This occurs at the point $(-1,1).$

The function covers all the $y$-values between $-3$ and $1,$ including both $-3$ and $1.$

Therefore, the range is $-3\le y\le 1,$ which can also be written as  $-3\le f(x)\le 1.$

Question 2
?

What is the range of the function f defined by the following table?

x −3 −2 −1 0 1 2
f(x) 0 −3 1 2 −1 4
a
{−3,−1,0,1,2,4}
b
{−3,−2,−1,0,1,2}
c
{0,1,2,4}
d
[−3,2]
e
[−3,4]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The range of f(x) consists of all the outputs that have a corresponding x-input.

In a table, the range consists of all numbers that feature in the row corresponding to f(x).

Therefore, the range is the set {−3,−1,0,1,2,4}.

x −3 −2 −1 0 1 2
f(x) 0 −3 1 2 −1 4
a

b
{−3,−2,−1,0,1,2}
c
{0,1,2,4}
d
[−3,2]
e
[−3,4]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The range of f(x) consists of all the outputs that have a corresponding x-input.

In a table, the range consists of all numbers that feature in the row corresponding to f(x).

Therefore, the range is the set {−3,−1,0,1,2,4}.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250894/assets/579e17e56674e39e552f1c0856f40e7f878ed94248a7a0e878c1f851c54ecbea.png)

What is the range of the function $f(x),$ shown above?
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the lowest and highest $y$-values in the graph.

- The lowest $y$-value is $-3.$ This occurs at the point $(3,-3).$

- The highest $y$-value is $1.$ This occurs at the point $(-1,1).$

The function covers all the $y$-values between $-3$ and $1,$ including both $-3$ and $1.$

question.html:
Question 3
?

What is the range of the function f(x), shown above?

a
−3≤f(x)≤0
b
1≤f(x)≤3
c
−3≤f(x)≤−1
d
−1≤f(x)≤3
e
−3≤f(x)≤1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the lowest and highest y-values in the graph.

  • The lowest y-value is −3. This occurs at the point (3,−3).

  • The highest y-value is 1. This occurs at the point (−1,1).

The function covers all the y-values between −3 and 1, including both −3 and 1.

Therefore, the range is −3≤y≤1, which can also be written as −3≤f(x)≤1.

question.html:
Question 3
?

What is the range of the function f(x), shown above?

a
−3≤f(x)≤0
b
1≤f(x)≤3
c
−3≤f(x)≤−1
d
−1≤f(x)≤3
e
−3≤f(x)≤1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the lowest and highest y-values in the graph.

  • The lowest y-value is −3. This occurs at the point (3,−3).

  • The highest y-value is 1. This occurs at the point (−1,1).

The function covers all the y-values between −3 and 1, including both −3 and 1.

Therefore, the range is −3≤y≤1, which can also be written as −3≤f(x)≤1.

solution.reasoning: The graph attains every output from -3 to 1. Both endpoints are filled, so both bounds are included: -3\le f(x)\le 1, option e. No captured Math Academy answer or grade confirms its key.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the lowest and highest $y$-values in the graph.

- The lowest $y$-value is $-3.$ This occurs at the point $(3,-3).$

- The highest $y$-value is $1.$ This occurs at the point $(-1,1).$

The function covers all the $y$-values between $-3$ and $1,$ including both $-3$ and $1.$

Therefore, the range is $-3\le y\le 1,$ which can also be written as  $-3\le f(x)\le 1.$

questions.name: Question 1
questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{m}{{n}^{2}m+2{n}^{2}}\cdot \frac{2m+4}{m}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{m}{{n}^{2}m+2{n}^{2}}\cdot \frac{2m+4}{m} & =\frac{m}{{n}^{2}(m+2)}\frac{2(m+2)}{m} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{m}}{{n}^{2}\cancel{(m+2)}}\frac{2\cancel{(m+2)}}{\cancel{m}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 2
questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{s-t}{s+3t}\cdot \frac{s+3t}{s-t}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{s-t}{s+3t}\cdot \frac{s+3t}{s-t} & =\frac{\cancel{(s-t)}}{\cancel{(s+3t)}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{(s+3t)}}{\cancel{(s-t)}} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}\cdot \frac{1}{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 3
questions.worked_solution:
We multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{m}^{3}}{2n}\cdot \frac{4{n}^{2}}{{m}^{2}} & =\frac{{m}^{3}\cdot 4{n}^{2}}{2n\cdot {m}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{m}^{3}{n}^{2}}{2n{m}^{2}} \\  & =2mn\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In the above example, we performed some cancellations after multiplying. However, with more complex expressions, it's often easier to cancel *before* multiplying.

Which of the following is equivalent to mn2m+2n2⋅2m+4m?

a
m2n2
b
2m2n
c
m32n2
d
2n2
e
2m3n
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

mn2m+2n2⋅2m+4m=mn2(m+2)2(m+2)m=mn2(m+2)2(m+2)m=2n2

question.name: Question 1
question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{m}{{n}^{2}m+2{n}^{2}}\cdot \frac{2m+4}{m}?$
question.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{m}{{n}^{2}m+2{n}^{2}}\cdot \frac{2m+4}{m} & =\frac{m}{{n}^{2}(m+2)}\frac{2(m+2)}{m} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{m}}{{n}^{2}\cancel{(m+2)}}\frac{2\cancel{(m+2)}}{\cancel{m}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Which of the following is equivalent to mn2m+2n2⋅2m+4m?

a
m2n2
b
2m2n
c
m32n2
d
2n2
e
2m3n
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

mn2m+2n2⋅2m+4m=mn2(m+2)2(m+2)m=mn2(m+2)2(m+2)m=2n2

Which of the following is equivalent to mn2m+2n2⋅2m+4m?

a
m2n2
b
2m2n
c
m32n2
d
2n2
e
2m3n
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

mn2m+2n2⋅2m+4m=mn2(m+2)2(m+2)m=mn2(m+2)2(m+2)m=2n2

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{m}{{n}^{2}m+2{n}^{2}}\cdot \frac{2m+4}{m}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{m}{{n}^{2}m+2{n}^{2}}\cdot \frac{2m+4}{m} & =\frac{m}{{n}^{2}(m+2)}\frac{2(m+2)}{m} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{m}}{{n}^{2}\cancel{(m+2)}}\frac{2\cancel{(m+2)}}{\cancel{m}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 3
question.worked_solution:
We multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{m}^{3}}{2n}\cdot \frac{4{n}^{2}}{{m}^{2}} & =\frac{{m}^{3}\cdot 4{n}^{2}}{2n\cdot {m}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{m}^{3}{n}^{2}}{2n{m}^{2}} \\  & =2mn\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In the above example, we performed some cancellations after multiplying. However, with more complex expressions, it's often easier to cancel *before* multiplying.

questions.problem:
What is the minor of ${x}_{12}$ in 
$X=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & 1 & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${x}_{12}$, we remove the $1$st row and $2$nd column:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 3 & ∗ & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & ∗ & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{12}=|\begin{aligned}3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.
$$

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 8 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & -7 & ∗ & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & ∗ & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & ∗ & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & ∗ & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

 

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{14}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -7 & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}|.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${f}_{13}$, we remove the $1$st row and $3$rd column:

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & 7 & ∗ & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & ∗ & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & ∗ & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & ∗ & 11 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

   

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{13}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 7 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 11 & 2\end{aligned}|.
$$

questions.worked_solution:

questions.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${g}_{42}$, we remove the $4$th row and $2$nd column: 

$$
G=[\begin{aligned}8 & ∗ & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & ∗ & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & ∗ & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ ∗ & \sqrt{5} & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ 11 & ∗ & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{42}=|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${g}_{42}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{42} & =(-1)^{4+2}{M}_{42} \\  & ={M}_{42} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 8
questions.problem:
Find the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ in 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${b}_{34}$, we remove the $3$rd row and the $4$th column: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{34}=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{34} & =(-1)^{3+4}{M}_{34} \\  & =-{M}_{34} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ in 
$X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 6 & -2 & 8 \\ -6 & 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${x}_{32}$, we remove the $3$rd row and $2$nd column: 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & ∗ & 2 & 0 \\ ∗ & 6 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{32}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|
$$

  

Therefore, the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}{M}_{32} \\  & =-{M}_{32} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${p}_{35}$, we remove the $3$rd row and $5$th column: 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 2 & 1 & ∗ \\ 3 & 5 & \sqrt{13} & 0 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -4 \\ 4 & 8 & 3 & 8 & ∗ \\ 11 & 3 & \sqrt{2} & -9 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{35}=|\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & \sqrt{13} & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 3 & 8 \\ 11 & 3 & \sqrt{2} & -9\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${p}_{35}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{35} & =(-1)^{3+5}{M}_{35} \\  & ={M}_{35} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & \sqrt{13} & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 3 & 8 \\ 11 & 3 & \sqrt{2} & -9\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 11
questions.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$S=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(S) & ={s}_{11}{C}_{11}+{s}_{12}{C}_{12}+{s}_{13}{C}_{13}+{s}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+2\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =2{C}_{12} \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & 2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 1 & ∗ & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & ∗ & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & ∗ & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}|) \\  & =-2((-5\cdot 2-4\cdot 2)-0+0) \\  & =-2\cdot (-18) \\  & =36\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 12
questions.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(W) & ={w}_{11}{C}_{11}+{w}_{12}{C}_{12}+{w}_{13}{C}_{13}+{w}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =1\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+5\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & ={C}_{11}+5{C}_{13} \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ ∗ & 3 & 0 & 4 \\ ∗ & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 5 & ∗ \\ 2 & 0 & ∗ & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & ∗ & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & ∗ & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|+5\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|+5|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|+5(2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 8 & -2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 8 & 0\end{aligned}|) \\  & =10(3\cdot (-2)-4\cdot 0) \\  & =10\cdot (-6) \\  & =-60\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 13
questions.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & ={a}_{11}{C}_{11}+{a}_{12}{C}_{12}+{a}_{13}{C}_{13}+{a}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+8\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =8{C}_{12} \\  & =8\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & 8 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -1 & ∗ & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & ∗ & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & ∗ & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =8(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-8((-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|) \\  & =8(6\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 2)-0+0 \\  & =8\cdot 14 \\  & =112\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 14
questions.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$W=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(W) & ={w}_{11}{C}_{11}+{w}_{12}{C}_{12}+{w}_{13}{C}_{13}+{w}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}+2\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =-{C}_{12}+2{C}_{14} \\  & =-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & -1 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & ∗ & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & ∗ & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & ∗ & 3 & 6\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & ∗ \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & ∗ \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & ∗\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}|+2\cdot (-1)^{4+1}|\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|-2(0\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|) \\  & =9-2\cdot (-5)\cdot 9 \\  & =9+90 \\  & =99\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 15
questions.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & -10 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -25\end{aligned}]$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & ={t}_{11}{C}_{11}+{t}_{12}{C}_{12}+{t}_{13}{C}_{13}+{t}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}-10\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =-10{C}_{14} \\  & =-10\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -10 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & ∗ \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & ∗\end{aligned}| \\  & =-10(-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =10(0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|) \\  & =10(0-4(1\cdot 3-1\cdot 2)+0) \\  & =10\cdot (-4) \\  & =-40\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Determinant of a NxN Matrix Using Cofactor Expansion

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
The minor of the entry $a_{ij}$ in a $n\times n$ matrix is the determinant that we get when the rows and columns containing $a_{ij}$ are removed.

For example, suppose that we wish to find the minor of $a_{32}$ in the following matrix:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14250940/assets/1fc0a03fc8f9611f5fa0385f597bbcaa563ed69076325f4dfa36f75067bc2c95.svg)

To get the minor of $a_{\color{red}{3}\color{blue}{2}}$, we remove the $\color{red}3$rd row and $\color{blue}2$nd column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & ∗ & 5 & 12 \\ ∗ & -2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -5 & ∗ & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of $a_{32}$, denoted $M_{32}$, is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14250940/assets/c76d128376d15417c8e4ef4c2a81452753415e1341b7e6214bd7f8dbdba48a50.svg)

We can now calculate the value of $M_{32}$ by evaluating the determinant using previously discussed methods.

tutorials.content:
The minor of the entry $a_{ij}$ in a $n\times n$ matrix is the determinant that we get when the rows and columns containing $a_{ij}$ are removed.

For example, suppose that we wish to find the minor of $a_{32}$ in the following matrix:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14250940/assets/1fc0a03fc8f9611f5fa0385f597bbcaa563ed69076325f4dfa36f75067bc2c95.svg)

To get the minor of $a_{\color{red}{3}\color{blue}{2}}$, we remove the $\color{red}3$rd row and $\color{blue}2$nd column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & ∗ & 5 & 12 \\ ∗ & -2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -5 & ∗ & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of $a_{32}$, denoted $M_{32}$, is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14250940/assets/c76d128376d15417c8e4ef4c2a81452753415e1341b7e6214bd7f8dbdba48a50.svg)

We can now calculate the value of $M_{32}$ by evaluating the determinant using previously discussed methods.

tutorials.name: Calculating a Cofactor of a NxN Matrix
tutorials.problem:
In general, for any $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ the **cofactor** $C_{ij}$ of the entry $\color{red}a_{ij}$ is

$$
{\color{blue}C_{ij}}=(-1)^{i+j}{\color{blue}M_{ij}}.
$$

Cofactors are a useful tool in helping us to compute determinants of larger matrices. Before we learn how, let's get some practice at computing cofactors.

tutorials.name: Calculating Determinants Using Cofactors
tutorials.problem:
One way to find the determinant of a $3\!\times\! 3$ matrix $A$ is to take the alternating sum of the entries of the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}M_{11}} - {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}M_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}M_{13}}
$$

Remember that we had to change the sign of the second product. When we multiply a minor of an entry by the respective sign in the formula like this, we get the cofactor of the entry. The cofactors in the above formula were ${\color{blue}M_{11}},$ $-{\color{blue}M_{12}},$ and ${\color{blue}M_{13}}.$

Using this idea, we can write the formula for the determinant of a $3\!\times\! 3$ matrix $A$ in terms of cofactors, as follows:

$$
\det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}C_{11}} + {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}C_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}C_{13}}
$$

This is called the **cofactor expansion** of the determinant across the first row.

In fact, we can use a similar method of multiplying the entries of the top row of the matrix by their respective cofactors to find the determinant for any $n\!\times\! n$ matrix $A$ when $n \ge 3$. The formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & ={\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{1j}{C}_{1j} \\  & ={a}_{11}{C}_{11}+{a}_{12}{C}_{12}+⋯+{a}_{1n}{C}_{1n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's see how to use this formula in the next example.

tutorial.content:
The minor of the entry $a_{ij}$ in a $n\times n$ matrix is the determinant that we get when the rows and columns containing $a_{ij}$ are removed.

For example, suppose that we wish to find the minor of $a_{32}$ in the following matrix:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14250940/assets/6bb0aa0a310373ffeadebade27bf6dfc95bf539c85d0e66c7d5667212846cdad.svg)

To get the minor of $a_{\color{red}{3}\color{blue}{2}}$, we remove the $\color{red}3$rd row and $\color{blue}2$nd column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & ∗ & 5 & 12 \\ ∗ & -2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -5 & ∗ & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of $a_{32}$, denoted $M_{32}$, is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14250940/assets/d6e139cd7f5bfdd3259ab89d69c7456499445a169d68ea9463d7fec0ea0d81c6.svg)

We can now calculate the value of $M_{32}$ by evaluating the determinant using previously discussed methods.

observed_steps.name: Question 1
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Minor in a NxN Matrix
observed_steps.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${x}_{12}$, we remove the $1$st row and $2$nd column:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 3 & ∗ & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & ∗ & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{12}=|\begin{aligned}3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.
$$

question.name: Question 1
question.problem:
What is the minor of ${x}_{12}$ in 
$X=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & 1 & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${x}_{12}$, we remove the $1$st row and $2$nd column:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 3 & ∗ & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & ∗ & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{12}=|\begin{aligned}3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 1
?

What is the minor of x12 in X=[501−23311721−88−641−2]?

a
|31171−8841−2|
b
|501331121−8|
c
|337218−64−2|
d
|01−231171−88|
e
|31172−88−61−2|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of x12, we remove the 1st row and 2nd column:

X=[∗0∗∗3∗1172∗−88−6∗1−2]

So, the minor is

M12=|31172−88−61−2|.

$$

Question 2
?

Find the minor of e14 in E=[3558513−700225−13−20−5380734252].

a
|3−7005−13−2−538034252|
b
|13−70225−1−20−53073452|
c
|13−70225−130−5387342|
d
|355813−70225−130−538|
e
|358513002253−20−58073252|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of e14, we remove the 1st row and 4th column:

E=[∗∗∗8∗13−7∗0225−1∗−20−53∗0734∗52]

So, the minor is M14=|13−70225−1−20−53073452|.

observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Minor in a NxN Matrix
observed_steps.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${f}_{13}$, we remove the $1$st row and $3$rd column:

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & 7 & ∗ & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & ∗ & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & ∗ & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & ∗ & 11 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

   

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{13}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 7 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 11 & 2\end{aligned}|.
$$

|0203184−15210−13112|

observed_steps.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${e}_{15}$, we remove the $1$st row and $5$th column:

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -7 & 0 & ∗ \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 & ∗ \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 & ∗ \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]

$$
{M}_{15}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 & 0 \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 5
?

Find the minor of e15 in E=[70−38512−70011543−20−508053−607].

a
−|70−3812−70115430−508|
b
−|12−70115430−50853−60|
c
−|0−3852−700543−2−5080|
d
|12−70115430−50853−60|
e
|0−3852−700543−2−5080|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of e15, we remove the 1st row and 5th column:

E=[∗∗∗∗512−70∗11543∗0−508∗53−60∗]

So, the minor is M15=|12−70115430−50853−60|.

tutorial.name: Calculating a Cofactor of a NxN Matrix
tutorial.problem:
In general, for any $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ the **cofactor** $C_{ij}$ of the entry $\color{red}a_{ij}$ is

$$
{\color{blue}C_{ij}}=(-1)^{i+j}{\color{blue}M_{ij}}.
$$

Cofactors are a useful tool in helping us to compute determinants of larger matrices. Before we learn how, let's get some practice at computing cofactors.

observed_steps.name: Question 6
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix
observed_steps.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${g}_{42}$, we remove the $4$th row and $2$nd column: 

$$
G=[\begin{aligned}8 & ∗ & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & ∗ & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & ∗ & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ ∗ & \sqrt{5} & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ 11 & ∗ & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{42}=|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${g}_{42}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{42} & =(-1)^{4+2}{M}_{42} \\  & ={M}_{42} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the cofactor of g42 in G=[8023−2350710−8−56−4453831130−911].

a
|823−230710−56−4110−911|
b
−|823−230710−56−4110−911|
c
|802−20−8−5−44533113011|
d
−|35010−8−5−44583113011|
e
−|802−20−8−5−44533113011|
Submit

EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of g42, we remove the 4th row and 2nd column:

G=[8∗23−23∗0710∗−56−4∗5∗∗∗11∗0−911]

So, the minor is

M42=|823−230710−56−4110−911|.

Now, the cofactor of g42 is

C42=(−1)4+2M42=M42=|823−230710−56−4110−911|.

$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{51}=|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${d}_{51}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{51} & =(-1)^{5+1}{M}_{51} \\  & ={M}_{51} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the cofactor of d51 in D=[−5−820135071−10−56−4406831130−93].

a
|−820150710−56−40683|
b
|3507−10−5640681130−9|
c
|−5−8203507−10−564068|
d
−|3507−10−5640681130−9|
e
−|−820150710−56−40683|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of d51, we remove the 5th row and 1st column:

D=[∗−8201∗5071∗0−56−4∗068311∗∗∗∗]

So, the minor is

M51=|−820150710−56−40683|.

Now, the cofactor of d51 is

C51=(−1)5+1M51=M51=|−820150710−56−40683|.

observed_steps.name: Question 8
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix
observed_steps.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${b}_{34}$, we remove the $3$rd row and the $4$th column: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{34}=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{34} & =(-1)^{3+4}{M}_{34} \\  & =-{M}_{34} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${x}_{32}$, we remove the $3$rd row and $2$nd column: 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & ∗ & 2 & 0 \\ ∗ & 6 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{32}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|
$$

  

Therefore, the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}{M}_{32} \\  & =-{M}_{32} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the cofactor of x32 in X=[05235020−56−28−6310].

a
 −|023520−610|

 −|0206−28310|

−|052502−56−2|

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of x32, we remove the 3rd row and 2nd column:

X=[0∗235∗20∗6∗∗−6∗10]

So, the minor is M32=|023520−610|

Therefore, the cofactor of x32 is C32=(−1)3+2M32=−M32=−|023520−610|.

Question 10
?

Find the cofactor of p35 in P=[3−8210351301−25−1−56−4483831132−97].

a
|3−8213513048381132−9|
b
|3−8103501−25−16−44883|
c
−|3−8103501−25−16−44883|
d
−|3−8213513048381132−9|
e
|51301−1−56−4838332−97|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of p35, we remove the 3rd row and 5th column:

P=[3−821∗35130∗∗∗∗∗−44838∗1132−9∗]

So, the minor is

M35=|3−8213513048381132−9|.

Now, the cofactor of p35 is

C35=(−1)3+5M35=M35=|3−8213513048381132−9|.

tutorial.name: Calculating Determinants Using Cofactors
tutorial.problem:
One way to find the determinant of a $3\!\times\! 3$ matrix $A$ is to take the alternating sum of the entries of the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}M_{11}} - {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}M_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}M_{13}}
$$

Remember that we had to change the sign of the second product. When we multiply a minor of an entry by the respective sign in the formula like this, we get the cofactor of the entry. The cofactors in the above formula were ${\color{blue}M_{11}},$ $-{\color{blue}M_{12}},$ and ${\color{blue}M_{13}}.$

Using this idea, we can write the formula for the determinant of a $3\!\times\! 3$ matrix $A$ in terms of cofactors, as follows:

$$
\det(A) = {\color{red}a_{11}}{\color{blue}C_{11}} + {\color{red}a_{12}}{\color{blue}C_{12}} + {\color{red}a_{13}}{\color{blue}C_{13}}
$$

This is called the **cofactor expansion** of the determinant across the first row.

In fact, we can use a similar method of multiplying the entries of the top row of the matrix by their respective cofactors to find the determinant for any $n\!\times\! n$ matrix $A$ when $n \ge 3$. The formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & ={\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{1j}{C}_{1j} \\  & ={a}_{11}{C}_{11}+{a}_{12}{C}_{12}+⋯+{a}_{1n}{C}_{1n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's see how to use this formula in the next example.

Question 1
?

What is the minor of x12 in X=[501−23311721−88−641−2]?

a
|31171−8841−2|
b
|501331121−8|
c
|337218−64−2|
d
|01−231171−88|
e
|31172−88−61−2|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of x12, we remove the 1st row and 2nd column:

X=[∗0∗∗3∗1172∗−88−6∗1−2]

So, the minor is

M12=|31172−88−61−2|.

last_observation.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${x}_{12}$, we remove the $1$st row and $2$nd column:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 3 & ∗ & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & ∗ & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{12}=|\begin{aligned}3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 1
?

What is the minor of x12 in X=[501−23311721−88−641−2]?

a
|31171−8841−2|
b
|501331121−8|
c
|337218−64−2|
d
|01−231171−88|
e
|31172−88−61−2|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of x12, we remove the 1st row and 2nd column:

X=[∗0∗∗3∗1172∗−88−6∗1−2]

So, the minor is

M12=|31172−88−61−2|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Minor in a NxN Matrix

solution.reasoning: The minor of x_{12} is the determinant obtained by deleting row 1 and column 2. The remaining rows are (3,11,7), (\sqrt{2},-8,8), and (-6,1,-2), matching option e. No captured answer or grade establishes Math Academy's key for this question.

feedback.name: Question 1
feedback.problem:
What is the minor of ${x}_{12}$ in 
$X=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & 1 & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${x}_{12}$, we remove the $1$st row and $2$nd column:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 3 & ∗ & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & ∗ & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{12}=|\begin{aligned}3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 1
?

What is the minor of x12 in X=[501−23311721−88−641−2]?

a
|31171−8841−2|
b
|501331121−8|
c
|337218−64−2|
d
|01−231171−88|
e
|31172−88−61−2|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of x12, we remove the 1st row and 2nd column:

X=[∗0∗∗3∗1172∗−88−6∗1−2]

So, the minor is

M12=|31172−88−61−2|.

question.name: Question 2
question.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${e}_{14}$, we remove the $1$st row and $4$th column:

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 8 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & -7 & ∗ & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & ∗ & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & ∗ & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & ∗ & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

 

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{14}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -7 & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 2
?

Find the minor of e14 in E=[3558513−700225−13−20−5380734252].

a
|3−7005−13−2−538034252|
b
|13−70225−1−20−53073452|
c
|13−70225−130−5387342|
d
|355813−70225−130−538|
e
|358513002253−20−58073252|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of e14, we remove the 1st row and 4th column:

E=[∗∗∗8∗13−7∗0225−1∗−20−53∗0734∗52]

So, the minor is M14=|13−70225−1−20−53073452|.

last_observation.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${e}_{14}$, we remove the $1$st row and $4$th column:

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 8 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & -7 & ∗ & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & ∗ & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & ∗ & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & ∗ & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

 

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{14}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -7 & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 2
?

Find the minor of e14 in E=[3558513−700225−13−20−5380734252].

a
|3−7005−13−2−538034252|
b
|13−70225−1−20−53073452|
c
|13−70225−130−5387342|
d
|355813−70225−130−538|
e
|358513002253−20−58073252|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of e14, we remove the 1st row and 4th column:

E=[∗∗∗8∗13−7∗0225−1∗−20−53∗0734∗52]

So, the minor is M14=|13−70225−1−20−53073452|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Minor in a NxN Matrix

solution.reasoning: Delete row 1 and column 4, retaining columns 1, 2, 3, and 5 of rows 2–5. The determinant of this remaining matrix is the minor, matching option b. No answer or grade for this current question is captured, so Math Academy's key remains unverified.

feedback.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${e}_{14}$, we remove the $1$st row and $4$th column:

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 8 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & -7 & ∗ & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & ∗ & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & ∗ & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & ∗ & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

 

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{14}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -7 & 0 \\ 22 & 5 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & 0 \\ 7 & 3 & 4 & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}|.
$$

To get the minor of ${f}_{13}$, we remove the $1$st row and $3$rd column:

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & 7 & ∗ & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & ∗ & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & ∗ & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & ∗ & 11 & 2\end{aligned}]

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{13}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 7 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 11 & 2\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 3
?

What is the minor of f13 in F=[0−15−22072031284−15−5210−143112]?

a
|−15−227203−521043112|
b
|0203184−15210−13112|
c
|0−152124−15−510−14112|
d
|7203284−1−521043112|
e
|0703124−15−510−14112|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of f13, we remove the 1st row and 3rd column: F=[∗∗5∗∗07∗0312∗4−15−5∗10−14∗112]

So, the minor is

M13=|0703124−15−510−14112|.

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Minor in a NxN Matrix
last_observation.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${f}_{13}$, we remove the $1$st row and $3$rd column:

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & 7 & ∗ & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & ∗ & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & ∗ & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & ∗ & 11 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

   

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{13}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 7 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 11 & 2\end{aligned}|.
$$

?

What is the minor of f13 in F=[0−15−22072031284−15−5210−143112]?

a
|−15−227203−521043112|
b
|0203184−15210−13112|
c
|0−152124−15−510−14112|
d
|7203284−1−521043112|
e
|0703124−15−510−14112|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of f13, we remove the 1st row and 3rd column: F=[∗∗5∗∗07∗0312∗4−15−5∗10−14∗112]

So, the minor is

M13=|0703124−15−510−14112|.

To get the minor of ${f}_{13}$, we remove the $1$st row and $3$rd column:

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 5 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & 7 & ∗ & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & ∗ & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & ∗ & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & ∗ & 11 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

   

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{13}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 7 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & -1 \\ 5 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & 11 & 2\end{aligned}|.
$$

question.problem:
Find the minor of ${c}_{11}$ in 
$C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ 17 & 13 & 5 & 5 \\ 8 & -9 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
To get the minor of of ${c}_{11}$, we remove the $1$st row and $1$st column:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ ∗ & 13 & 5 & 5 \\ ∗ & -9 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{11}=|\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 1 \\ 13 & 5 & 5 \\ -9 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}|.
$$

Find the minor of c11 in C=[3−40507011713558−92−2].

a
|7011355−92−2|
b
|070171358−92|
c
|3−4007017135|
d
|−4051355−92−2|
e
|3−450718−9−2|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of of c11, we remove the 1st row and 1st column: C=[3∗∗∗∗701∗1355∗−92−2] So, the minor is M11=|7011355−92−2|.

feedback.name: Question 4
feedback.problem:
Find the minor of ${c}_{11}$ in 
$C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ 17 & 13 & 5 & 5 \\ 8 & -9 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
To get the minor of of ${c}_{11}$, we remove the $1$st row and $1$st column:

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ ∗ & 13 & 5 & 5 \\ ∗ & -9 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{11}=|\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 1 \\ 13 & 5 & 5 \\ -9 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}|.
$$

To get the minor of ${e}_{15}$, we remove the $1$st row and $5$th column:

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -7 & 0 & ∗ \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 & ∗ \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 & ∗ \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]

$$
{M}_{15}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 & 0 \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 5
?

Find the minor of e15 in E=[70−38512−70011543−20−508053−607].

a
−|70−3812−70115430−508|
b
−|12−70115430−50853−60|
c
−|0−3852−700543−2−5080|
d
|12−70115430−50853−60|
e
|0−3852−700543−2−5080|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of e15, we remove the 1st row and 5th column:

E=[∗∗∗∗512−70∗11543∗0−508∗53−60∗]

So, the minor is M15=|12−70115430−50853−60|.

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -7 & 0 & ∗ \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 & ∗ \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 & ∗ \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
{M}_{15}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 & 0 \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}|.

Question 5
?

Find the minor of e15 in E=[70−38512−70011543−20−508053−607].

a
−|70−3812−70115430−508|
b
−|12−70115430−50853−60|
c
−|0−3852−700543−2−5080|
d
|12−70115430−50853−60|
e
|0−3852−700543−2−5080|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To get the minor of e15, we remove the 1st row and 5th column:

E=[∗∗∗∗512−70∗11543∗0−508∗53−60∗]

So, the minor is M15=|12−70115430−50853−60|.

feedback.worked_solution:
To get the minor of ${e}_{15}$, we remove the $1$st row and $5$th column:

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -7 & 0 & ∗ \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 & ∗ \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 & ∗ \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

 

So, the minor is

$$
{M}_{15}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 & 0 \\ 11 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 & 8 \\ 5 & 3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Question 6
?

Find the cofactor of g42 in G=[8023−2350710−8−56−4453831130−911].

a
|823−230710−56−4110−911|
b
−|823−230710−56−4110−911|
c
|802−20−8−5−44533113011|
d
−|35010−8−5−44583113011|
e
−|802−20−8−5−44533113011|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of g42, we remove the 4th row and 2nd column:

G=[8∗23−23∗0710∗−56−4∗5∗∗∗11∗0−911]

So, the minor is

M42=|823−230710−56−4110−911|.

Now, the cofactor of g42 is

C42=(−1)4+2M42=M42=|823−230710−56−4110−911|.

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${g}_{42}$, we remove the $4$th row and $2$nd column: 

$$
G=[\begin{aligned}8 & ∗ & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & ∗ & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & ∗ & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ ∗ & \sqrt{5} & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ 11 & ∗ & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{42}=|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${g}_{42}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{42} & =(-1)^{4+2}{M}_{42} \\  & ={M}_{42} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Find the cofactor of g42 in G=[8023−2350710−8−56−4453831130−911].

a
|823−230710−56−4110−911|
b
−|823−230710−56−4110−911|
c
|802−20−8−5−44533113011|
d
−|35010−8−5−44583113011|
e
−|802−20−8−5−44533113011|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of g42, we remove the 4th row and 2nd column:

G=[8∗23−23∗0710∗−56−4∗5∗∗∗11∗0−911]

So, the minor is

M42=|823−230710−56−4110−911|.

Now, the cofactor of g42 is

C42=(−1)4+2M42=M42=|823−230710−56−4110−911|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix

solution.reasoning: The cofactor is C_{42}=(-1)^{4+2}M_{42}=M_{42}. Delete row 4 and column 2, retaining rows 1, 2, 3, and 5 and columns 1, 3, 4, and 5. The resulting determinant matches option a. No captured answer or grade verifies Math Academy's key for this question.

feedback.name: Question 6
feedback.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${g}_{42}$, we remove the $4$th row and $2$nd column: 

$$
G=[\begin{aligned}8 & ∗ & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & ∗ & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & ∗ & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ ∗ & \sqrt{5} & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ 11 & ∗ & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{42}=|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${g}_{42}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{42} & =(-1)^{4+2}{M}_{42} \\  & ={M}_{42} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

question.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${d}_{51}$, we remove the $5$th row and $1$st column: 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}∗ & -8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ ∗ & 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ ∗ & 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ ∗ & 0 & 6 & 8 & 3 \\ 11 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{51}=|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${d}_{51}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{51} & =(-1)^{5+1}{M}_{51} \\  & ={M}_{51} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Find the cofactor of d51 in D=[−5−820135071−10−56−4406831130−93].

a
|−820150710−56−40683|
b
|3507−10−5640681130−9|
c
|−5−8203507−10−564068|
d
−|3507−10−5640681130−9|
e
−|−820150710−56−40683|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of d51, we remove the 5th row and 1st column:

D=[∗−8201∗5071∗0−56−4∗068311∗∗∗∗]

So, the minor is

M51=|−820150710−56−40683|.

Now, the cofactor of d51 is

C51=(−1)5+1M51=M51=|−820150710−56−40683|.

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${d}_{51}$, we remove the $5$th row and $1$st column: 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}∗ & -8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ ∗ & 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ ∗ & 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ ∗ & 0 & 6 & 8 & 3 \\ 11 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{51}=|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${d}_{51}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{51} & =(-1)^{5+1}{M}_{51} \\  & ={M}_{51} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Find the cofactor of d51 in D=[−5−820135071−10−56−4406831130−93].

a
|−820150710−56−40683|
b
|3507−10−5640681130−9|
c
|−5−8203507−10−564068|
d
−|3507−10−5640681130−9|
e
−|−820150710−56−40683|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of d51, we remove the 5th row and 1st column:

D=[∗−8201∗5071∗0−56−4∗068311∗∗∗∗]

So, the minor is

M51=|−820150710−56−40683|.

Now, the cofactor of d51 is

C51=(−1)5+1M51=M51=|−820150710−56−40683|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix

solution.reasoning: The cofactor is C_{51}=(-1)^{5+1}M_{51}=M_{51}. Deleting row 5 and column 1 gives the determinant in option a, with a positive sign. No captured answer or grade verifies Math Academy's key for this question.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${d}_{51}$, we remove the $5$th row and $1$st column: 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}∗ & -8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ ∗ & 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ ∗ & 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ ∗ & 0 & 6 & 8 & 3 \\ 11 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{51}=|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${d}_{51}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{51} & =(-1)^{5+1}{M}_{51} \\  & ={M}_{51} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 8
question.problem:
Find the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ in 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${b}_{34}$, we remove the $3$rd row and the $4$th column: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{34}=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{34} & =(-1)^{3+4}{M}_{34} \\  & =-{M}_{34} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

a
−|−223130−700|
b
|−22002−2−703|
c
−|−22013502−2|
d
|−22013502−2|
e
|−230105−703|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of b34, we remove the 3rd row and the 4th column:

B=[−223∗130∗∗∗∗−2−700∗]

So, the minor is M34=|−223130−700|.

Therefore, the cofactor of b34 is

C34=(−1)3+4M34=−M34=−|−223130−700|.

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${b}_{34}$, we remove the $3$rd row and the $4$th column: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{34}=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{34} & =(-1)^{3+4}{M}_{34} \\  & =-{M}_{34} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

B=[−223∗130∗∗∗∗−2−700∗]

C34=(−1)3+4M34=−M34=−|−223130−700|.

feedback.name: Question 8
feedback.problem:
Find the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ in 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${b}_{34}$, we remove the $3$rd row and the $4$th column: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -2 \\ -7 & 0 & 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{34}=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$

Therefore, the cofactor of ${b}_{34}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{34} & =(-1)^{3+4}{M}_{34} \\  & =-{M}_{34} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ -7 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 9
question.problem:
Find the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ in 
$X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 6 & -2 & 8 \\ -6 & 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${x}_{32}$, we remove the $3$rd row and $2$nd column: 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & ∗ & 2 & 0 \\ ∗ & 6 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{32}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|
$$

  

Therefore, the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}{M}_{32} \\  & =-{M}_{32} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find the cofactor of x32 in X=[05235020−56−28−6310].

a
 −|023520−610|
b
 −|0206−28310|
c
−|052502−56−2|
d
 |023520−610|
e
|052502−56−2|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of x32, we remove the 3rd row and 2nd column:

X=[0∗235∗20∗6∗∗−6∗10]

So, the minor is M32=|023520−610|

Therefore, the cofactor of x32 is C32=(−1)3+2M32=−M32=−|023520−610|.

last_observation.name: Question 9
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${x}_{32}$, we remove the $3$rd row and $2$nd column: 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & ∗ & 2 & 0 \\ ∗ & 6 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{32}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|
$$

  

Therefore, the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}{M}_{32} \\  & =-{M}_{32} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 9
?

Find the cofactor of x32 in X=[05235020−56−28−6310].

a
 −|023520−610|
b
 −|0206−28310|
c
−|052502−56−2|
d
 |023520−610|
e
|052502−56−2|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of x32, we remove the 3rd row and 2nd column:

X=[0∗235∗20∗6∗∗−6∗10]

So, the minor is M32=|023520−610|

Therefore, the cofactor of x32 is C32=(−1)3+2M32=−M32=−|023520−610|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix

solution.reasoning: Delete row 3 and column 2 to obtain the minor with rows (0,2,3), (5,2,0), and (-6,1,0). The cofactor sign is (-1)^{3+2}=-1, so option a is correct. No captured answer or grade verifies Math Academy's key for this question.

feedback.problem:
Find the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ in 
$X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 6 & -2 & 8 \\ -6 & 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${x}_{32}$, we remove the $3$rd row and $2$nd column: 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & ∗ & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & ∗ & 2 & 0 \\ ∗ & 6 & ∗ & ∗ \\ -6 & ∗ & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{32}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|
$$

  

Therefore, the cofactor of ${x}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}{M}_{32} \\  & =-{M}_{32} \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ -6 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Question 10
?

Find the cofactor of p35 in P=[3−8210351301−25−1−56−4483831132−97].

a
|3−8213513048381132−9|
b
|3−8103501−25−16−44883|
c
−|3−8103501−25−16−44883|
d
−|3−8213513048381132−9|
e
|51301−1−56−4838332−97|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of p35, we remove the 3rd row and 5th column:

P=[3−821∗35130∗∗∗∗∗−44838∗1132−9∗]

So, the minor is

M35=|3−8213513048381132−9|.

Now, the cofactor of p35 is

C35=(−1)3+5M35=M35=|3−8213513048381132−9|.

last_observation.name: Question 10
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, to get the minor of ${p}_{35}$, we remove the $3$rd row and $5$th column: 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 2 & 1 & ∗ \\ 3 & 5 & \sqrt{13} & 0 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -4 \\ 4 & 8 & 3 & 8 & ∗ \\ 11 & 3 & \sqrt{2} & -9 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor is 

$$
{M}_{35}=|\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & \sqrt{13} & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 3 & 8 \\ 11 & 3 & \sqrt{2} & -9\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, the cofactor of ${p}_{35}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}_{35} & =(-1)^{3+5}{M}_{35} \\  & ={M}_{35} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 5 & \sqrt{13} & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 3 & 8 \\ 11 & 3 & \sqrt{2} & -9\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Find the cofactor of p35 in P=[3−8210351301−25−1−56−4483831132−97].

a
|3−8213513048381132−9|
b
|3−8103501−25−16−44883|
c
−|3−8103501−25−16−44883|
d
−|3−8213513048381132−9|
e
|51301−1−56−4838332−97|
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of p35, we remove the 3rd row and 5th column:

P=[3−821∗35130∗∗∗∗∗−44838∗1132−9∗]

So, the minor is

M35=|3−8213513048381132−9|.

Now, the cofactor of p35 is

C35=(−1)3+5M35=M35=|3−8213513048381132−9|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Cofactor in a NxN Matrix

|51301−1−56−4838332−97|

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, to get the minor of p35, we remove the 3rd row and 5th column:

question.name: Question 11
question.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$S=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(S) & ={s}_{11}{C}_{11}+{s}_{12}{C}_{12}+{s}_{13}{C}_{13}+{s}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+2\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =2{C}_{12} \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & 2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 1 & ∗ & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & ∗ & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & ∗ & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}|) \\  & =-2((-5\cdot 2-4\cdot 2)-0+0) \\  & =-2\cdot (-18) \\  & =36\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$S=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(S) & ={s}_{11}{C}_{11}+{s}_{12}{C}_{12}+{s}_{13}{C}_{13}+{s}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+2\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =2{C}_{12} \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & 2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ 1 & ∗ & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & ∗ & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & ∗ & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}|) \\  & =-2((-5\cdot 2-4\cdot 2)-0+0) \\  & =-2\cdot (-18) \\  & =36\end{aligned}
$$

$$

We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(W) & ={w}_{11}{C}_{11}+{w}_{12}{C}_{12}+{w}_{13}{C}_{13}+{w}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =1\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+5\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & ={C}_{11}+5{C}_{13} \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ ∗ & 3 & 0 & 4 \\ ∗ & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 5 & ∗ \\ 2 & 0 & ∗ & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & ∗ & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & ∗ & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|+5\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|+5|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|+5(2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 8 & -2\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 8 & 0\end{aligned}|) \\  & =10(3\cdot (-2)-4\cdot 0) \\  & =10\cdot (-6) \\  & =-60\end{aligned}

question.name: Question 15
question.problem:
Calculate the determinant of the matrix
$T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & -10 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -25\end{aligned}]$
question.worked_solution:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & ={t}_{11}{C}_{11}+{t}_{12}{C}_{12}+{t}_{13}{C}_{13}+{t}_{14}{C}_{14} \\  & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13}-10\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =-10{C}_{14} \\  & =-10\cdot |\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & -10 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & ∗ \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & ∗ \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & ∗\end{aligned}| \\  & =-10(-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =10(0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|) \\  & =10(0-4(1\cdot 3-1\cdot 2)+0) \\  & =10\cdot (-4) \\  & =-40\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Suppose we have a vector $\overrightarrow{AB}=\textbf{a}.$ We denote its **magnitude**, also known as its *modulus* or *length*, as $|\overrightarrow{AB}|$ or $|\textbf{a}|.$

For example, the vector below has a magnitude of $8,$ denoted $|\overrightarrow{AB}|=8.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/71105c9d5920ec71e61fe1176021024188a86bd8023671b79e0ce89082994299.png)

Now, let's consider the following situation. Suppose that the vector $\textbf{a}$ is directed vertically upwards and $|\textbf{a}|=6,$ while $\textbf{b}$ is directed horizontally to the right and $|\textbf{b}|=8.$ How can we find $|\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}|?$

First, we use the triangle law of addition to find the resultant $\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/ffd155d3b72015a72d878fc8089381a5bcf5a97f698f85945642189ea7368a3f.png)

Notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\text{a}+\text{b}{|}^{2} & =|\text{a}{|}^{2}+|\text{b}{|}^{2} \\  & ={6}^{2}+{8}^{2} \\  & =100\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}|=\sqrt{100}=10.
$$

**Important**: In the above calculation we wrote $|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|^2 = |\mathbf{a}|^2+|\mathbf{b}|^2$. This works only when the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are at right angles, and the relationship is not true in general. We'll see how to deal with non-right-angled vectors soon.

tutorials.name: Calculating the Magnitude of a Vector Using the Law of Cosines
tutorials.problem:
When the triangle law for addition does *not* give a right triangle, we *cannot* use the Pythagorean theorem to compute the magnitude of the sum.

For example, using the triangle law to draw the sum $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ for the vectors below, we do not get a right triangle. Instead, we get a triangle with an obtuse angle $\theta.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/967966ec9d8ac0b7358623645de0e7931ef4d6cc87bd919d1f0cf04f7ca6ca28.png)

We do not obtain a right triangle here, so we cannot use the Pythagorean theorem. However, we can use the law of cosines:

$$
\begin{aligned}{|a+b|}^{2} & ={|a|}^{2}+{|b|}^{2}-2|a||b|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

In general, given any two vectors that form a triangle using the triangle addition law, we can always use the law of cosines to compute the magnitude of the sum.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/967966ec9d8ac0b7358623645de0e7931ef4d6cc87bd919d1f0cf04f7ca6ca28.png)

We do not obtain a right triangle here, so we cannot use the Pythagorean theorem. However, we can use the law of cosines:

$$
\begin{aligned}{|a+b|}^{2} & ={|a|}^{2}+{|b|}^{2}-2|a||b|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

In general, given any two vectors that form a triangle using the triangle addition law, we can always use the law of cosines to compute the magnitude of the sum.

tutorial.name: Introduction
tutorial.problem:
Suppose we have a vector $\overrightarrow{AB}=\textbf{a}.$ We denote its **magnitude**, also known as its *modulus* or *length*, as $|\overrightarrow{AB}|$ or $|\textbf{a}|.$

For example, the vector below has a magnitude of $8,$ denoted $|\overrightarrow{AB}|=8.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/71105c9d5920ec71e61fe1176021024188a86bd8023671b79e0ce89082994299.png)

Now, let's consider the following situation. Suppose that the vector $\textbf{a}$ is directed vertically upwards and $|\textbf{a}|=6,$ while $\textbf{b}$ is directed horizontally to the right and $|\textbf{b}|=8.$ How can we find $|\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}|?$

First, we use the triangle law of addition to find the resultant $\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/ffd155d3b72015a72d878fc8089381a5bcf5a97f698f85945642189ea7368a3f.png)

Notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\text{a}+\text{b}{|}^{2} & =|\text{a}{|}^{2}+|\text{b}{|}^{2} \\  & ={6}^{2}+{8}^{2} \\  & =100\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\textbf{a}+\textbf{b}|=\sqrt{100}=10.
$$

**Important**: In the above calculation we wrote $|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}|^2 = |\mathbf{a}|^2+|\mathbf{b}|^2$. This works only when the vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are at right angles, and the relationship is not true in general. We'll see how to deal with non-right-angled vectors soon.

question.problem: In rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=18$ and $BC=9.$ Find $|\overset{\to }{BD}|.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/3e03c8d3377aef27d7542ef2d734ebd64d00bbc1539e63222b7df9abc696bd44.png)

As we can see from the picture above, in $△BAD$ we have $∠BAD={90}^{∘}$, $AB=18$ and $AD=BC=9.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem gives

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{BD}| & =BD \\  & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}+A{D}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{18}^{2}+{9}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{405} \\  & =9\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $|\overset{\to }{BD}|=9\sqrt{5}.$

feedback.problem: In rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=18$ and $BC=9.$ Find $|\overset{\to }{BD}|.$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251078/assets/3e03c8d3377aef27d7542ef2d734ebd64d00bbc1539e63222b7df9abc696bd44.png)

$$

$$

Hence, $|\overset{\to }{BD}|=9\sqrt{5}.$

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬(A∨B))\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for the part of the expression that's in parentheses, $A∨B:$ 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∨B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |

| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Next, we add the column for $A∧¬(A∨B):$ 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∨B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)\,$ | $\,A∧¬(A∨B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Finally, we add the column for $¬(A∧¬(A∨B))):$ 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∨B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)\,$ | $\,A∧¬(A∨B)\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬(A∨B))\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨(P∧¬Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's add columns for $¬P$ and $¬Q:$

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Then, we add a column for the part of the expression that's in parentheses, $P∧¬Q:$

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ | $\,P∧¬Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Finally, we add a column for $¬P∨(P∧¬Q):$

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬P\,$ | $\,¬Q\,$ | $\,P∧¬Q\,$ | $\,¬P∨(P∧¬Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)∧A\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we add a column for the part of the expression that's in parentheses, $A∨B:$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Then, we add a column for the negation, $¬(A∨B):$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∨B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Finally, we add a column for $¬(A∨B)∧A:$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∨B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)\,$ | $\,¬(A∨B)∧A\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |

questions.worked_solution:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ |

| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Finally, we add the column for $¬(A∧¬(A∧B))):$

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,B∨(¬A∧¬B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-4}} |
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's add columns for $¬A$ and $¬B:$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬A\,$ | $\,¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Then, we add a column for the part of the expression that's in parentheses, $¬A∧¬B:$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬A\,$ | $\,¬B\,$ | $\,¬A∧¬B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Finally, we add a column for $B∨(¬A∧¬B):$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬A\,$ | $\,¬B\,$ | $\,¬A∧¬B\,$ | $\,B∨(¬A∧¬B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

questions.name: Question 6
questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

 

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q){{field-4}}Q
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(P∨Q)∧¬(P\text{ }∧¬Q) & ≡(\text{T}∨\text{T})∧¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q) & ≡(\text{T}∨\text{F})∧¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q) & ≡(\text{F}∨\text{T})∧¬(\text{F}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q)$ is logically equivalent to $Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{F}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q)≡Q.
$$

questions.name: Question 7
questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(P∨Q){{field-4}}¬P∨Q
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∨Q) & ≡¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬P∨Q & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∨Q) & ≡¬(\text{F}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬(P∨Q)$ is logically equivalent to $¬P∨Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are *different* (one is $\text{F},\text{F},\text{F},\text{T}$, while the other is $\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{T}$). Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(P∨Q)\text{⧸}≢¬P∨Q.
$$

questions.name: Question 8
questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧(B∨¬A)\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
A∧(B∨¬A){{field-4}}A∧B
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∧(B∨¬A) & ≡\text{T}∧(\text{T}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧(\text{T}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∧B & ≡\text{T}∧\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∧(B∨¬A) & ≡\text{F}∧(\text{T}∨¬\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∧(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧(B∨¬A)\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $A∧(B∨¬A)$ is logically equivalent to $A∧B,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.  

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{F},\text{F},\text{F}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
A∧(B∨¬A)≡A∧B.
$$

questions.name: Question 9
questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(A∧¬B){{field-4}}¬A∨B
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧¬B) & ≡¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{T}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬A∨B & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧¬B) & ≡¬(\text{F}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{F}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below. 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬(A∧¬B)$ is logically equivalent to $¬A∨B,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{T}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(A∧¬B)≡¬A∨B.
$$

\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{F})∨¬(\text{T}∨¬\text{F}) \\  & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{F})∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{F}∧\text{T})∨¬(\text{F}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)$ is logically equivalent to $A,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

We see that the columns for $(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)$ and $A$ are different. They differ in the second and third rows. Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)≢A.
$$
