EXPLANATION

Using a cofactor expansion along the 4th column, we have

|52−3931−20210032−10|=9⋅C14+0⋅C24+0⋅C34+0⋅C44=9⋅(−1)1+4⋅|31−221032−1|=−9⋅|31−221032−1|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column

solution.reasoning: Expanding along column 4 leaves only the entry 9 in row 1. Its cofactor sign is (-1)^{1+4}=-1. Deleting row 1 and column 4 yields exactly the minor in option b, with coefficient -9. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different matrix.

feedback.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 & 9 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =9\cdot {C}_{14}+0\cdot {C}_{24}+0\cdot {C}_{34}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =9\cdot (-1)^{1+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-9\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 14
question.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 7 & 4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{13}+4\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{2+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -3 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -3 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column
last_observation.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 7 & 4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{13}+4\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{2+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -3 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -3 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

?

|1−101174−1−3501−2−10−2|=

a
|1−11−351−2−1−2|
b
4⋅|1−11−351−2−1−2|

−|1−11−351−2−1−2|

−2⋅|1−11−351−2−1−2|
e
−4⋅|1−11−351−2−1−2|
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using a cofactor expansion along the 3rd column, we have

|1−101174−1−3501−2−10−2|=0⋅C13+4⋅C23+0⋅C33+0⋅C43=4⋅(−1)2+3⋅|1−11−351−2−1−2|=−4⋅|1−11−351−2−1−2|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column

solution.reasoning: Expanding along column 3 leaves only the entry 4 in row 2. Its cofactor sign is (-1)^{2+3}=-1, giving -4 times the determinant obtained by deleting row 2 and column 3, exactly option e. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different matrix.

feedback.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 7 & 4 & -1 \\ -3 & 5 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{13}+4\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{2+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -3 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -3 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.name: Question 15
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column
last_observation.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{14}+5\cdot {C}_{24}+0\cdot {C}_{34}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =5\cdot (-1)^{2+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Using a cofactor expansion along the 4th column, we have

|3−140202512001240|=0⋅C14+5⋅C24+0⋅C34+0⋅C44=5⋅(−1)2+4⋅|3−14120124|=5⋅|3−14120124|.
question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column

solution.reasoning: Expanding along column 4 leaves only the entry 5 in row 2. Its cofactor sign is (-1)^{2+4}=1. Deleting row 2 and column 4 yields exactly the minor in option a, with coefficient 5. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different matrix.

feedback.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{14}+5\cdot {C}_{24}+0\cdot {C}_{34}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =5\cdot (-1)^{2+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
